cards.text: The LORD has a burden, a word for Israel, the people He chose as His own (Deuteronomy 7:6), and it comes through a man named Malachi. Chosen? I KNOW that feeling, because somebody picked me out of a clearance bin for 25 cents and I still haven't gotten over it.

cards.question: Here come the LORD's first words to Israel through Malachi. What does He tell them?
Israel hears the LORD say “I have loved you” and takes it right in, no questions asked.

cards.text: Nope, Israel fires right back: “How have You loved us?” That's like telling somebody “I love you” and they look up from their phone and go, “Okay, send me the receipts.”
So the LORD answers with a question of His own: “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother?” Esau and Jacob were twin sons of Isaac (Genesis 25:24-26), and later God renamed Jacob as Israel (Genesis 35:10).

cards.question: The LORD is talking to Israel, the people who came from Jacob. Which one does He say He has loved?

cards.text: Jacob. Then the LORD says, “but Esau I have hated,” and He points to what's become of Esau's land.

cards.question: The LORD says He has made Esau's mountains a ___ and left his inheritance to the desert jackals.

cards.text: Edom, Esau's people (Genesis 36:9), may say, “We have been devastated, but we will rebuild the ruins,” and honestly, I respect that. When MY edges wore down, I got slid into the back of a junk drawer and didn't even TRY to climb out.

cards.question: Edom plans to rebuild the ruins. What does the LORD of Hosts say about that?

answers.text: He will tear down what they build
He will help them build it back
He will let them build in peace

cards.question: The LORD says He will be indignant with Edom for only a little while.

cards.text: Forever, and Edom will be called the Land of Wickedness. “You will see this with your own eyes,” the LORD tells Israel.

cards.question: Israel will see all this for themselves. What does the LORD say they will end up saying about Him?

answers.text: He is great even beyond Israel
He is great only inside Israel
He has stepped away from Israel

cards.text: That's it, they'll say, “The LORD is great—even beyond the borders of Israel.” My greatness stops at the edge of one little cookie planet, and the OVEN gets most of the credit.
